title: Pushing Against Nothing
question: How can a rocket speed up where there is no air to push against?
hook: A rocket speeds up in the emptiest place there is, with nothing around it to push on.
idea: A rocket throws exhaust out fast and carries everything it burns, so it needs no air and works better outside the atmosphere.

beats.prompt: A rocket has left the atmosphere and is in the vacuum of space. Its engine keeps running. What happens?

choices.label: It stops speeding up, because there is nothing to push against
choices.feedback: It tempts because we imagine a vehicle pushing on something around it, but a rocket gets thrust from the exhaust it expels.

choices.label: It keeps speeding up, and its engine works more efficiently there
It slows down as it runs short of oxygen from the air
choices.feedback: This is true of jet engines, but a rocket carries all its propellant and needs no oxygen from air.

beats.explain: A rocket engine makes thrust by reaction to exhaust expelled at high speed, so it needs no surrounding air and operates more efficiently outside the atmosphere.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in the history of military rockets in order.
items: Gunpowder rockets evolve in China under the Song dynasty
Iron-cased rockets are developed in the Kingdom of Mysore
Rocket artillery accuracy is greatly increased by William Hale
beats.explain: Gunpowder rockets date to the 13th century, Mysorean rockets to the late 18th, the Congreve rocket to 1804 and Hale's improvement to 1844.

beats.prompt: Match each person to what they did in rocket history.
pairs: Gave the first mathematical treatment of rocket propulsion
Designed a British rocket based on Mysorean rockets
First proposed rockets for human spaceflight
Conceived that idea later and built a body of theory on it
beats.explain: Each of them moved rockets from a weapon toward a subject of mathematics and space travel.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A jet engine burns its fuel with oxygen taken from the air.
A rocket carries all its propellant and does not need air.
So a rocket should work best in thick air, where there is more to push on.
So a rocket can fly in the vacuum of space.
beats.explain: Rocket engines actually operate more efficiently outside the atmosphere, because they do not push on surrounding air.
